narrative:
The model predicts you have a 42% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your chances of success.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have indicated you do not want to pursue higher education. Among students who passed, every single one expressed a desire to continue studying after school; your lack of that ambition strongly pulls the prediction toward failure. The second most important factor is that you have had no previous class failures, which actually works in your favor and pushes the outcome slightly toward passing. The third notable influence is your 30-to-60-minute commute to school. Most students who passed live much closer, with over 60% traveling less than 15 minutes, so your longer travel time adds a moderate push toward the failing outcome.

To improve, you should seriously reflect on your goals. If you can find motivation to aim for further education, that shift alone could dramatically change your trajectory. At the same time, explore ways to reduce travel burden or use that time more productively for study. Even small, consistent increases in weekly study time and attendance could build the momentum you currently lack. Taking the remedial courses seriously gives you a practical opportunity to address these gaps before the final exams.
